title: Design CI/CD Pipeline for Java Microservices
question: Design complete CI/CD pipeline for 20 Java microservices. Requirements: 1) Automated build on every commit, 2) Run unit tests, integration tests, security scans, 3) Build Docker images, 4) Deploy to dev/staging/production environments, 5) Blue-green deployment for production, 6) Rollback capability, 7) Parallel builds for independent services. Discuss: using GitHub Actions or Jenkins for CI, triggering builds on push to feature branches, running Maven/Gradle build with unit tests, using Testcontainers for integration tests, scanning dependencies with OWASP Dependency Check, using SonarQube for code quality, building Docker images with multi-stage builds, pushing to container registry (ECR/Docker Hub), using Kubernetes for deployment, implementing GitOps with ArgoCD/Flux, deploying to dev automatically, requiring approval for staging/prod, using blue-green deployment with Kubernetes services, implementing canary deployment for gradual rollout, using Helm for templating, monitoring deployments with Prometheus/Grafana, implementing rollback by switching service traffic, and using matrix builds for parallel service builds.

title: Optimize Docker Images for Production
question: Optimize Docker images to reduce size and build time. Requirements: 1) Current image: 800MB, build time 10 minutes, 2) Reduce image size for faster deployments, 3) Reduce build time for faster feedback, 4) Maintain security best practices, 5) Layer caching for efficiency. Discuss: using multi-stage builds (build stage with full JDK, runtime stage with JRE only), using slim/alpine base images (openjdk:17-jre-slim vs openjdk:17), copying only necessary files (.dockerignore for excluding unnecessary files), ordering Dockerfile commands (stable layers first: OS packages, then dependencies, then application code), using layer caching (copy pom.xml first, download dependencies, then copy source code), implementing dependency caching with BuildKit, using distroless images for minimal attack surface, scanning images with Trivy/Snyk, running as non-root user, minimizing layers with command chaining, removing build-time dependencies from final image, and using Docker BuildKit for parallel stage execution.

title: Production Kubernetes Cluster Setup
question: Set up production-ready Kubernetes cluster. Requirements: 1) High availability (no single point of failure), 2) Auto-scaling based on CPU/memory, 3) Load balancing across pods, 4) Persistent storage for databases, 5) Secrets management, 6) Monitoring and logging, 7) Network policies for security. Discuss: using managed Kubernetes (EKS, GKE, AKS) for control plane HA, setting up multi-zone cluster for node redundancy, configuring Horizontal Pod Autoscaler based on metrics, implementing cluster autoscaler for node scaling, using service type LoadBalancer or Ingress for external traffic, configuring readiness and liveness probes for health checks, using StatefulSets for stateful applications, provisioning PersistentVolumes with StorageClass, using external-secrets or sealed-secrets for secret management, implementing RBAC for access control, using network policies to restrict pod communication, setting up Prometheus and Grafana for monitoring, configuring log aggregation with ELK/Loki, implementing resource requests and limits for QoS, using pod disruption budgets for high availability, and implementing disaster recovery with Velero.

title: Implement Zero-Downtime Deployment
question: Achieve zero-downtime deployment for critical application. Requirements: 1) Application serves 10K requests/second, 2) Deploy multiple times per day, 3) No service interruption during deployment, 4) Rollback within seconds if issues detected, 5) Database schema changes without downtime. Discuss: using blue-green deployment (maintain two identical environments, switch router after deployment), implementing canary deployment (gradually shift traffic from old to new), using rolling updates in Kubernetes (deploy new pods, wait for ready, then terminate old), implementing health checks to ensure new version is healthy before switching traffic, using feature flags to enable/disable features without deployment, handling database migrations with backward-compatible changes (expand-migrate-contract pattern: add new column, deploy code using both, migrate data, remove old column), implementing database views for schema abstraction, using load balancer health checks to remove unhealthy instances, implementing graceful shutdown (drain connections before pod termination), using readiness gates to control traffic switching, monitoring error rates and latency during deployment, and implementing automatic rollback based on metrics.
